question: Can actual Timestral beat LightGBM, XGBoost and a physical solar model, with stronger baselines checked?

stage_1.selection_metric: largest relative development MAE reduction against the best of six comparators

stage_1_candidate_rule: First 20 plants in native June Parquet order passing first-14-day qualification: 672 rows, >=650 valid resource flags, >=150 valid readings >100 W/m2, complete nonnegative measured power. No August data used.
stage_1_result: RNMB06 was the only June candidate beating all six comparators by MAE; 8.6606% gain. The selected 5M/four-covariate model lost July validation (3.586077 vs best baseline 3.032351 MW).

stage_2.selection_metric: lowest combined June 15 through July 31 MAE among six Timestral size/input variants at the June-selected plant
stage_2.prior_attempt: 5M with four covariates selected from 20 June plants lost July validation; July is now development, not test

stage_2_variants: 5M and 28M, each with target only, calendar only, or all four benchmark covariates. Select lowest combined June 15-July 31 MAE, with no August ranking or hyperparameter tuning.
availability_repairs: During August execution, the final two origins lacked a valid same-clock resource reading within 14 days. Extend only the weather fallback to older pre-issue readings. The final origin had zero Q95 power among resource-valid calibration rows: retain the most recent informative tree/physical calibration. All 31 August days remain scored. These engineering changes followed input/fit failures before the full August score was computed; this is not a preregistered untouched-pipeline trial.
interpretation: Descriptive one-plant historical comparison. August Timestral MAE is lower than all six listed comparators, but its 0.0048% edge over Daily median is a practical tie, and Daily mean has lower RMSE. No universal superiority or statistical-significance claim. Unknown pretraining overlap.
